subtitle: Integrated Math and Science for ArchitectureIV
courseType:

keywords: Power series expansion of functions 2.Differential equations
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) power series expansion of functions (Maclaurin series) (2) differential equations
advice: This is a basic course in calculus for students in the Dept. of Architecture. We will cover the following topics: 1. Power series expansion of functions 2. Differential equations 3. Integration issues (deflection curve equation) Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students. Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises after each class. Extra materials may be distributed if necessary. Students are required to show their solution/calculation procedure logically and clearly in each assignment. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.
books: Textbooks:Integrated Math and Science for Architecture III IV [Kanazawa Institute of Technology] Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and skills from Integrated Math and Science for Architecture I, II, III.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic concepts of Taylor/Maclaurin series and find Maclaurin series of basic functions.
Be able to solve separable, linear first order and homogeneous linear second order differential equations.
Be able to explain various problems in architecture using differential equations.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all topics, attend all classes, and complete all required work.
Understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics.
